newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end higher with focus on small-caps.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end higher with focus on small-caps.

text.p: Retail buying of second-line shares helped the market to a positive finish, but institutional money was again kept sidelined by continuing currency worries, analysts said.
"Only the speculative stocks and second liners are moving. On the blue chips, I don't see much," said a dealer at a bank-owned brokerage house.
The key Composite Index of large-capitalised stocks rose 2.20 points to 1,031.61.
Timber stock Evermaster typified the surge of speculative issues.
The stock gained 3.10 ringgit or 17.65 percent to 22.50.
Other stocks targeted by retail buyers included property stocks Berjaya Land and Eupe and timber concern Seal, which rose between six cents to 1.10 ringgit.
Analysts said lingering concerns over stability of the ringgit were uppermost in the minds of institutional funds.
"The market's very much determined by movements in currencies. Valuations are dirt cheap but that's not the primary concern," said S.J. Securities chief analyst Faez Khairuddin.
Analysts said the market's upside is limited.
